headline: A startup called Outlit is pitching companies on AI agents that follow each customer's calls and social media posts to find ways to sell to them.
score_reason: Satirical-tone commentary on a startup pitch, no deployment figures; pool score kept.
importance_line: It would affect customers whose calls and public posts are profiled, and raises privacy questions, but the details come only from the startup's own pitch.
summary: Futurism reports, as relayed by Gizmodo, that startup Outlit offers businesses AI agents that watch customers almost around the clock, reading call logs and public social media posts to build profiles and plans for upselling and winning back lost leads. Founder Josh Earle told Futurism that the practice is legal; Gizmodo's piece is critical commentary and questions what 'anonymized' means for such profiles.
notes: Source chain: Futurism (first reporter) via Gizmodo; Futurism link not seen, url is the Gizmodo page.
